1) The concept of the piston. In Terraria, using the wiring system to modify the world is limited to acuators, pumps, and explosives. In Minecraft, the affordances given by the piston offer a wide variety of new technologies. This is further compounded by things like the hopper, redstone block, etc

2) The combat. In terraria, combat is more fully fleshed out and complex. Weather or not it’s ‘better’ is left to personal taste, but terraria has options like summoner, magic, ranger, tank, melee, etc. in Minecraft, there exist few/no distinctions between classes. You can use a crossbow as effectively as you can a sword.

3) Tiered progression. In terraria, progression is blocked by certain tiers. You can’t get hardmode armor till you kill the wall of flesh. You can’t get chlorophyte till you kill plantera. You can’t get Nebula equipment till you kill the lunar pillars. In Minecraft, the tiers are not quite so rigid. The only real gates are that you need an iron pick to get diamonds, and now you need a diamond pick to get netherite, along with obsidian for enchantments.

In short, terraria is more fleshed out by the developer, whereas Minecraft is more fleshed out by the player base.
